scope: Offline ARM9 inspection only; no ROM, code, save, or runtime mutation.

extraction_and_tools.method: Read ARM9 with existing ndspy NintendoDSRom API and decompressed ARM9 buffer. Temporary ELF wrapper was used only to disassemble selected raw ARM9 addresses with the installed LLVM objcopy/objdump; no new parser or ROM write was made.
extraction_and_tools.whole_arm9_comparison: The target and immediate parent ARM9 buffers are identical. Clean Plus/base ARM9 buffers differ in size and whole-buffer hash, but all listed getter/setter wrapper, dispatch, table-entry and field-114 case ranges are byte-identical across all four ROMs.

case.block_resolution: The generic dispatcher obtains substructure index 1 into r6 before the field switch; its source layout identifies substructure index 1 as PokemonDataBlockB.
The generic dispatcher obtains substructure index 1 into r5 before the field switch; its source layout identifies substructure index 1 as PokemonDataBlockB.
case.effect: Writes the supplied 16-bit value directly to PokemonDataBlockB+0x1A; the case does not mask, validate, or preserve subfields itself.

target_internal_helpers.getter_resolution: Mapped from the Party GetMonDataInternal default call at 0x0206E58E and the four substructure pointer loads plus field switch matching pinned PokeHeartGold pokemon.c:481-488.
target_internal_helpers.setter_resolution: Mapped from the Party SetMonDataInternal default call at 0x0206EDC0 and the four substructure pointer loads plus field switch matching pinned PokeHeartGold pokemon.c:972-988.

box_helpers.reference_mapping: Pinned retail PokeHeartGold source maps GetBoxMonData/SetBoxMonData field 114 to blockB.unused2 at +0x1A (getter pokemon.c:728-732; setter pokemon.c:1190-1194). Party getters/setters delegate non-party fields to these corresponding BoxMon internal functions (pokemon.c:410-460 and 886-951).
box_helpers.wrapper_limit: The outer target GetBoxMonData/SetBoxMonData wrapper entry points were not independently symbol-mapped in this bounded pass. The internal field-dispatch functions and Party fallback routes are byte-backed; this does not certify every PC/daycare live path or its outer checksum/decryption wrapper.
box_helpers.next_step: If global availability requires proving all Box paths, resolve outer BoxMon wrapper callsites and audit PC/daycare callers separately; the field-114 internal getter/setter mapping itself is established.

mask_ownership.reason: The accessor case operates on the whole u16 and contains no mask-specific validation. Exact matching getter/setter bytes only establish the storage mapping; they do not show whether another target consumer owns bits 1-5.
not_examined: all ARM9 and overlay references to raw field offsets

conclusion: The exact target Party getter/setter and their BoxMon internal field dispatchers map field 114 to the same 16-bit blockB+0x1A word as retail. This resolves the storage mapping, not global availability of mask 0x003E or every outer BoxPokemon runtime path. Nature implementation remains gated on a separate ownership/consumer audit.
